ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a hemispherical bowl with smooth inner wall and rim is fixed on a horizontal plane, and the rim of the bowl remains horizontal. Ball A, ball C, and ball B are respectively connected by two light thin strings. When the system remains at rest, ball B has just no pressure on the bowl wall; in the figure $\theta=30^\circ$. Find the ratio of the masses of ball A and ball C.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a hemispherical bowl fixed on a horizontal plane, with the rim of the bowl represented by a horizontal dashed line. The left and right endpoints of the bowl rim can be denoted as L and R. Ball A hangs vertically near the left end, and ball C hangs vertically near the right end; ball B is inside the bowl near the right side, and two light thin strings respectively connect from the left end L and the right end R to B. The θ marked in the figure is the angle between the left slanted line LB and the horizontal bowl rim LR, and the problem gives θ=30°. Reasoning: According to the geometric relation in the figure, L and R are the two endpoints of the semicircular bowl rim, and B is on the semicircular wall, so since the inscribed angle subtending a semicircle is a right angle, ∠LBR=90°. Since LB makes θ=30° with the horizontal LR, the right string BR makes 90°−θ=60° with the horizontal line. Let the tensions of the left and right strings on B be T_A and T_C respectively. Since ball B has just no pressure on the bowl wall, in the horizontal direction B is balanced only by the horizontal components of the tensions of the two strings, so T_A cosθ = T_C cos(90°−θ)=T_C sinθ. Therefore T_A/T_C = sinθ/cosθ = tanθ = tan30° = 1/√3. The bowl rim is smooth, the strings are light, and A and C hang at rest, so T_A=m_A g, T_C=m_C g. Hence m_A/m_C = T_A/T_C = 1/√3, that is, the ratio of the masses of ball A and ball C is 1:√3.
